segments.text: This ordinary house is seven problems away from surviving a blackout.
But the power's out, and the fridge is warming up. So we keep the door shut. A full freezer holds for two days, a fridge only four hours.
But it's pitch black. So we hang battery lanterns. Not candles, they start house fires.
But phones die fast. So we stash a charged power bank in the drawer.
But the water pump needs power too. So we fill the tub and bottles before the outage, one gallon per person, per day.
But now it's getting cold. So we shrink the house to one room, and layer up with blankets.
But a generator makes carbon monoxide. So it runs outside, at least twenty feet from the house, with a detector inside.
But the internet is down. So we add a hand-crank radio for official updates.
Seven problems. Seven fixes. One ordinary house, ready for the dark.
